correctness.rationale: For a three-vertex principal block, the determinant identity \(\det R=(1-x^2)(1-y^2)-(z-xy)^2\) makes the conditional LKJ density even about \(z=xy\), so \(\mathbb E[z\mid x,y]=xy\). Hansen's exact pairwise independence and variance \(\mathbb E[x^2]=1/\nu\) then give the triangle moment \(\nu^{-2}\). For any nontriangle set of three distinct edges, some graph vertex has odd degree, and conjugation by the corresponding diagonal sign matrix reverses the product while preserving the LKJ law, forcing expectation zero. The cubic trace is then the sum over ordered distinct vertex triples. I independently re-expanded the determinant and checked the normalization at representative parameters.

value.rationale: The theorem pinpoints the first obstruction hidden beyond an exact pairwise-independence result and converts it into an explicit finite-dimensional spectral statistic that matches the third centered moment of the limiting law. This is a natural structural statistic of the LKJ ensemble, not a parameter-only restatement.

final_claim:
For \(C\sim\operatorname{LKJ}_n(\eta)\), \(n\ge3\), \(\eta>0\), and \(
u=n+2\eta-1\), the product moment of three distinct off-diagonal entries equals \(
u^{-2}\) exactly when their edges form a triangle and is zero otherwise; hence \(\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}((C-I_n)^3)=n(n-1)(n-2)/
u^2\).
limitations: Only this third-order statistic is classified; no full higher-cumulant theory or fluctuation theorem is claimed.
The asymptotic Marchenko--Pastur comparison in the package concerns \(\eta_n/n\) converging to a finite nonnegative limit.
